Daily Digest · Computer Science

LLM Agents Scale Up: Trust, Tools, and Embodied Reasoning

Today's papers chart the maturation of language model agents from orchestration security to embodied robotics. The dominant theme is grounding—whether through tool reliability, multimodal alignment, or physical simulation—as researchers move beyond text-only reasoning toward systems that must operate reliably in real environments. A particularly striking trend: the shift from fine-tuning isolated models to full-pipeline adaptation, where agents learn from human videos and interact with distributed knowledge systems.

AI Safety
Fuzzing the LLM-Tool Trust Boundary Automatically

ToFu automatically derives semantic security checks for LLM tools from metadata, addressing the critical gap where tool semantics go unenforced when LLMs generate arguments. This matters because as agents orchestrate external tools, malformed or adversarial inputs can cascade into system-level failures.

ToFu uses CWE-guided sanitizers to specialize security checks per tool, closing a previously underexplored attack surface in agentic systems.
Islam Ananto, Prevost-Avenel et al. 2610.13651 PDF
Robotics
Pre-trained Robot Policies Learn from Human Video Supervision

LAPT-Scale sidesteps the expensive embodied robot data collection problem by learning latent actions from large-scale human egocentric videos, then adapting those priors to actual robot tasks. This dramatically scales generalist robot policies without requiring millions of robot interactions.

Latent action pre-training on human videos transfers effectively to downstream robotic manipulation with minimal real-world finetuning.
Xiang, Liu et al. 2610.13732 PDF
Computer Vision
Physically Grounded 3D Assets via Multi-Agent Simulation

Artisan extends asset generation from appearance to physics, using multi-agent pipelines with physical simulation feedback to create 3D objects that not only look right but move, balance, and collide realistically. This bridges the gap between geometric generation and functional digital twins.

The system generates collision-free articulated motion with accurate mass and material properties by integrating procedural generation with physics validation loops.
Cai, Zhu et al. 2610.13947 PDF
Machine Learning
Cross-Modal Latent Alignment in Independent Image Generators

InstantFusion discovers that independently trained diffusion/flow models exhibit similar latent spatial organization and can hand off intermediate states between architectures. This enables seamless model composition and cross-model adaptation without retraining.

Heterogeneous generators share an intrinsic latent compatibility that permits direct intermediate state transfer, enabling unified inference pipelines across model families.
Dai, Bu et al. 2610.13944 PDF

ToFu: Exploiting and Fuzzing the LLM-Orchestrator-Tool Trust Boundary

Introduces ToFu, a framework that automatically derives semantic security checks for LLM-orchestrated tools from metadata and CWE-guided sanitizers. Addresses the vulnerability where LLM-generated arguments bypass tool-level enforcement, enabling systematic fuzzing of this critical interface.

Proposes OpenPA, an automatic pronunciation assessment framework leveraging Whisper's cross-attention to jointly predict word- and utterance-level scores without forced alignment. Demonstrates end-to-end learning across heterogeneous transcription settings.

Featured Researcher
XK
Xuhui Kang
Roboticist · Embodied AI

Kang specializes in adapting pre-trained robot policies to new tasks with limited data, focusing on representation alignment under distribution shift. His work bridges vision-language models and embodied manipulation, particularly through retrieval-anchored methods that preserve generalization. Featured today for RARA's innovative approach to robust policy fine-tuning, which addresses a critical pain point in scaling robot learning: maintaining learned priors while adapting to novel environments.
